Access the Customizing Implementation Model for Application Systems (IMG) by navigating to 'SAP Menu' > 'Tools' > " IMG" from any transaction code window or execute query RSPAR075X in Transaction Code S_ALPHA_SWPM if your system is on Netweaver 2.x/Java stack, which includes BW and ECC systems Step-by-step guide: Setting ROIDOCPRMS parameter via IMG activities for both Business Warehouse (BW) & Enterprise Central Component(ECC ) in a landscape as shown below; this will ensure optimized performance of Extractions across multiple packages without causing any short dumps due incorrect configuration related package size settings. - In the 'IMG' screen, navigate to "Logistics" > ⟶ “SAP NetWeaver” --> Configuration'' tab where all available options regarding Parameter setting are displayed under various categories like Data Dictionary Parameters Maintenance etcetera depending upon whether you want change only for ECC or BW landscape respectively - Select the appropriate activity group corresponding to your requirement i.e 'Maintenance of data dictionary parameters' if changes need be applied just on an individual basis else choose global option accordingly so that it propagates throughout entire system landscapes comprising both Business Warehouse(BW) & Enterprise Central Components (ECC ) systems - Within selected Activity Group, look for Parameter Name as "ROIDOCPRMS" under which lies our target field 'Value'. texts.full_text: constellation On Mathworld it is stated that a prime constellation refers specifically, though not exclusively or exhaustively so, to certain sets within the set {p_n} where p_k = k-th smallest number in an increasing sequence of primes (or some other strictly monotonic series). These can include things like: - A pair: consecutive primes. Also called "twin" pairs - Cousins : twin + 4 or maybe something else, i.e., {5,k+6} - Triples and higher sequences where a difference between two elements of the sequence is fixed. This general term also appears to be used more specifically for: The four consecutive primes which contain only three distinct residues mod p. This was first shown by Hardy & Littlewood and further examples can include: - Prime quadruples - Primes with certain differences, e.g., prime triples that differ by 6k. I'd like to ask a question about the above definition: How many sequences exist where all members of {p_n} are not necessarily consecutive
